target_customer: Institutional asset managers and other buy side firms that route equity orders through an agency broker and its execution algorithms
problem: Buy side firms felt that broker execution algorithms were opaque and conflicted, with little transparency into how orders were handled.
business_model: Agency broker-dealer earning commissions per share on institutional equity executions
product_category: Institutional equities agency broker and execution algorithm platform

founders.name: Daniel Aisen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Search results describe both founders as former IEX executives but the cited article was not opened, so prior employers are left empty.

founders.name: Allison Bishop
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. Background not verified from an opened source.

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a low latency order routing and algorithm platform, connectivity to exchanges and clearing, and a FINRA registered broker-dealer; the company reports FINRA approval in July 2020 and first live trade in January 2021.

defensibility.rationale: A broker-dealer license and clearing connections take time to obtain, but execution algorithms are a crowded field dominated by large banks.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not determined from the sources opened; the company remains independent per the YC page and later Medium updates.

market_need_then: Buy side demand for execution transparency is described by the company and trade press, but no dated evidence of spend was opened in this research.

identity.voice_and_tone: Transparent and candid, with progress updates and a post titled 'Reasons not to try Proof'

branding.brand_signature: Public progress update series on Medium and an open engineering blog
branding.community_and_virality: Regular Medium progress updates and trade press such as Waters Technology and Business Insider coverage of Allison Bishop.

brand_strength.rationale: Name signals rigor and a candid blog builds credibility in a niche market, but the brand is known mainly among institutional traders.

outcome_analysis: Proof Trading launched as a small agency broker-dealer with founders from the exchange world, obtained FINRA approval in mid-2020 and made its first live trade in January 2021 per search summaries of its updates, and added senior hires by 2023. It stays active with 7 people per YC. Funding details could not be verified, so its success cannot be scored on raised capital.
